cf.title: Honor fillfactor in sorted GiST builds

input.subject: [PATCH] reduce page overlap of GiST indexes built using sorted method

verdict_reasoning: The goal stands: the patch makes a documented GiST reloption work again for sorted builds, and no surviving objection disputes it. Two fixable measurement gaps remain. maintenance-fit-1 asks for an unpatched baseline at the default fillfactor, and maintenance-fit-2 asks for the 2022 query benchmarks rerun on patched indexes. Confidence is low because the v1 patch prose is not in the material and both objections rest on missing numbers.

brief.title: Honor fillfactor in sorted GiST index builds
brief.problem: Since commit f1ea98a79 (2022), sorted GiST builds ignore the fillfactor reloption, so the index size does not change with fillfactor. Alexander Lakhin found that a regression test meant to rebuild with a different fillfactor does nothing, and that docs and release notes never mentioned the change. This affects users who set fillfactor on GiST indexes whose opclass has sortsupport.
brief.proposed_design: The patch treats fillfactor as a soft limit when the sorted build recursively partitions the buffered tuples into pages. A page may go over the limit when the opclass split would otherwise create a page with one tuple. Ordinary GiST page splits after the build do not change.
user_visible_surface: The fillfactor reloption on GiST indexes now affects the size of indexes built with the sorted method.
Index size after create index or reindex changes for GiST opclasses with sortsupport and a non-default fillfactor.
author_claims: Supporting fillfactor is better than documenting sorted builds as an exception, more so as more opclasses provide sortsupport.
With 20,000 points, fillfactor 90 gave 220 pages and fillfactor 40 gave 442 pages.
A test covers large INCLUDE tuples at fillfactor 10.
Ordinary GiST page splits are unchanged.
brief.thread_state: Andrey Borodin posted v1 in August 2026 and asked whether it should go to the CommitFest, with no reply visible. The same day's Coverity issue in gist_indexsortbuild() and its Assert-only patch is a separate item.
unclear: The thread does not show how the default GiST fillfactor changes the size of existing sorted-built indexes after reindex or upgrade.
The patch gives no query time or page overlap numbers, which the 2022 change was made to improve.
The patch gives no build time numbers before and after.
The patch prose, touched files and any documentation hunk for v1-0001-Honor-fillfactor-in-sorted-GiST-builds.patch are not included.
The thread does not say whether the change is for master only or for back branches.

objections.title: Default fillfactor would change every sorted-built GiST index
objections.failure_scenario: A PostGIS user who never set fillfactor upgrades and runs reindex. Their index is now built under the default GiST fillfactor of 90 as a soft limit, where today the setting is ignored. Index size and page overlap both change, and the user first sees it as a larger index or a different query plan cost.
objections.argument: The patch helps users who set a non-default fillfactor, but the default applies to every GiST index with sortsupport, so most of the effect lands on people who never asked for it. Message #17 reports 220 pages at fillfactor 90 and 442 at 40, but gives no baseline for unpatched master. Without that baseline a reviewer cannot tell whether default builds stay the same size. The thread also does not say whether the change is for master only.
objections.author_must_show: For the same data and the default fillfactor, how do index size and page count compare between unpatched master and the patch?

critic.reasoning: Message #14 shows the current sorted build gives the same size at fillfactor 40 and 100, so the default of 90 has no effect today. Message #17 gives no unpatched baseline, so the material cannot show that default builds keep their size.

objections.title: No query or overlap numbers for the change to the 2022 partitioning
objections.failure_scenario: The soft fillfactor limit cuts into the picksplit-based partitioning that f1ea98a79 added to reduce page overlap. If the new page boundaries raise overlap, spatial joins on rebuilt indexes slow down. The 2022 thread reported a slowdown of about 2 times in a self-join for the old sorted build, and nobody would notice a regression like that until queries slow down in production.
objections.argument: Messages #1, #4 and #12 justified the current algorithm with query timings and overlap statistics. The v1 patch in message #17 changes the same partitioning step but reports only page counts. Andrey Borodin noted in message #2 that picksplit makes an exact fillfactor impossible, so the soft limit interacts with picksplit in ways that page counts alone do not show. Few people know this code, and the visible thread shows no reviewer for v1.
objections.author_must_show: With the 2022 benchmarks rerun, do the self-join and tiling query times on patched default-fillfactor indexes match those on current master?

critic.reasoning: The patch changes the partitioning step that f1ea98a79 justified with query timings in messages #1, #4 and #12. Message #17 reports only page counts, so it does not show that overlap and query time are preserved.

refuted.title: No measurement shows honoring fillfactor helps sorted GiST indexes
refuted.failure_scenario: A user reindexes a GiST index whose opclass has sortsupport, keeping the default fillfactor. With the patch the index may come out larger than before. The user pays in disk space and cache with no measured gain in query or insert time, and notices only after the reindex or upgrade.
refuted.argument: The two GIN fillfactor attempts were rejected because no benchmark showed the option improved performance [P6][P8]. Message #17 gives page counts only, with no query, insert-split or build time numbers. The author argues from consistency with the documented option, and the option already exists for GiST, so this is weaker than adding a new knob. Message #14 offers a cheaper path: document the exception or drop fillfactor support for sorted builds.
refuted.author_must_show: With default and low fillfactor, how do size, query time and later insert splits of a sorted-built GiST index compare before and after the patch?

critic.reasoning: [P6] and [P8] rejected a new GIN reloption. Here fillfactor is an existing, documented GiST option that sorted builds honored in Postgres 14 (message #14). The remaining concerns about default-fillfactor size and missing query numbers duplicate maintenance-fit-1 and maintenance-fit-2.

refuted.title: Default fillfactor 90 silently changes every sorted GiST rebuild
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who never set fillfactor upgrades and runs reindex on a PostGIS or point GiST index. The default of 90 now applies, so the rebuilt index is larger and its page layout differs from the release before. The user notices only when disk use or scan timings move after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: Since f1ea98a79, sorted builds have ignored fillfactor, including the default (message #14). Message #17 reports sizes for 90 and 40 but not for the current no-fillfactor behaviour against the default, and it gives no query or overlap numbers. That overlap was the reason for the 2022 change (message #1). The cost falls on every user of a sortsupport opclass, while the gain goes to the few who set a non-default value.
refuted.author_must_show: How do size, build time and query time of a sorted GiST index with default fillfactor compare before and after the patch?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1 for the default-fillfactor size change, and of maintenance-fit-2 for the missing query and overlap numbers. [P8] concerned a new GIN option and should not be used as support.

refuted.title: Dormant fillfactor settings in dumps start to apply after restore
refuted.failure_scenario: A site set fillfactor = 10 on a GiST index years ago, and it has had no effect since Postgres 15. pg_dump emits the reloption, and restore or pg_upgrade plus reindex into the patched release builds an index several times larger. The site finds out when the disk fills or the restore runs long.
refuted.argument: The reloption has been kept in the catalog and in dumps through four or more major releases while doing nothing for sorted builds. Under the patch it takes effect with no action from the user. The thread does not say whether the patch is for master only (message #17). If it were backpatched, a minor release would change index size with no warning. The patch prose does not include a release-note or documentation hunk that tells users to check existing settings.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the change master-only, and what will the release notes and docs tell users who have long-ignored fillfactor settings on GiST indexes?

critic.reasoning: A user who set fillfactor = 10 gets the documented behaviour that Postgres 14 and the buffering build already give, which is not a failure. The CommitFest entry targets PG20 and no message proposes a backpatch, so the minor-release case is speculative.

refuted.title: buffering = on already gives a GiST build that honors fillfactor
refuted.failure_scenario: A user who wants free space in a GiST index can set `buffering = on` or `off` today, and the build then honors fillfactor. The patch adds a second fillfactor path to the sorted build that future work on gist_indexsortbuild() must keep correct. If no user needs a sorted build that also leaves free space, that cost buys little.
refuted.argument: Message #14 notes that fillfactor still works for the buffering build, and the sorted build runs only when `buffering` is auto and every key has sortsupport. So a user who wants a non-default fillfactor can get it now, at the cost of a slower build: message #1 measured about 3 to 6 times slower than the sorted build. Message #17 says supporting fillfactor beats documenting an exception, but it shows no user who needs both a fast build and free space.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users need a sorted GiST build with non-default fillfactor, and why is `buffering = on` plus a documented exception not enough for them?

critic.reasoning: The scenario names a maintenance cost but no concrete failure. Item 12 points the other way here: the buffering build and Postgres 14 sorted builds honor fillfactor, so the patch removes a departure from existing practice and adds no new user surface.

refuted.title: No user has asked for fillfactor in sorted GiST builds
refuted.failure_scenario: The build code gains a soft fillfactor limit, and future changes to the sorted build must keep it working. Meanwhile no workload is shown where a lower fillfactor helps a sortsupport GiST index. Reviewers find out only later whether anyone sets the option.
refuted.argument: The only trigger is message #14, where a regression test was found to do nothing; it is not a field report. Message #15 notes no field complaints about this code in four years, and the thread shows no user asking for fillfactor here. The page counts in message #17 show the index grows; they do not show fewer splits or faster inserts afterwards. The recorded reason in [P8] and [P6], that fillfactor is only worth adding with benchmarks showing a benefit, applies directly.
refuted.author_must_show: Which insert-heavy workload on a sortsupport GiST index runs faster or bloats less after the build when fillfactor is below the default?

critic.reasoning: [P6] and [P8] asked for benchmarks before adding a new option, but this patch makes an existing documented option work again after f1ea98a79 silently disabled it. Message #15's "lack of field complaints" refers to a null dereference and says nothing about fillfactor demand.

refuted.title: Default fillfactor may grow every sorted-built GiST index
refuted.failure_scenario: A PostGIS user who never set fillfactor upgrades and reindexes. If the GiST default of 90 is now honored, the index is larger and uses more shared_buffers. The few users who set fillfactor get the gain.
refuted.argument: Message #14 shows that sorted builds currently pack pages the same at any fillfactor, so the default is ignored today as well. The proposal does not say whether the default now applies. The brief lists the same gap as open. If it applies, the cost falls on all sortsupport GiST users, and message #6 notes that a lower fillfactor wastes space both on disk and in shared_buffers.
refuted.author_must_show: How much larger does a sortsupport GiST index get with the default fillfactor after this patch, compared with today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which states the same default-fillfactor concern and asks for the unpatched baseline.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-1: Default fillfactor would change every sorted-built GiST index

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The patch restores behaviour lost in 2022, and the thread does not say whether it is for master only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The sorted build in gistbuild.c gains a soft fillfactor limit that later changes to the partitioning step must keep working.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the picksplit-based partitioning that decides page overlap, and so scan time, for every sorted-built GiST index.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: For the same data and the default fillfactor, how do index size and page count compare between unpatched master and the patch?
With the 2022 benchmarks rerun, do the self-join query times on patched default-fillfactor indexes match those on current master?
How does create index time for a sorted GiST build compare before and after the patch?
Is the change for master only, or is a backpatch proposed?
What will the docs and release notes tell users whose GiST fillfactor settings have had no effect since the 2022 change?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the GiST build code, in particular the sorted build and its picksplit-based partitioning in gistbuild.c.
committability.liability: The owner signs for index size and scan performance of every sorted-built GiST index after reindex, including PostGIS indexes, for as long as the sorted build exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author moved the entry to the next CommitFest in October 2026 and took part in the 2022 work on the same code.

priority.reason: Only users who set a non-default fillfactor on sortsupport GiST indexes gain, and the change adds no new user surface. Review cost is a guess because the v1 patch was not read; the open points are measurements the author can supply.

provisional_note: The v1 patch, its touched files and any documentation hunk are not in the material. Whether the soft limit preserves the 2022 partitioning at the default fillfactor can only be judged from the code and new measurements.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Speeding up GIST index builds using popcount
precedents_retrieved.summary: Patch 0001 makes hemdistsign() in tsgistidx.c and similar GiST code XOR the signature bitvectors in 64-bit chunks and count bits with popcount64, which speeds up GiST index builds on tsvector by about 12-50% depending on siglen. Patch 0002 removes the pg_popcount32/64 function pointer on non-x86 platforms so that calls go directly to __builtin_popcount.
precedents_retrieved.objection: John Naylor declined to pass 0002 to a committer because of its code complexity, and said full asm popcount support on Arm would be the better approach. For 0001, he asked the author to measure whether the earlier 1-7% regression at small default siglen still exists before applying it in all contrib modules, and the pointer alignment question was still being worked on. The author's last message (August 2021) promised replies to the other review comments, and no revised patch appears before the entry was returned in October.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Readability counts, and as it stands I don't feel comfortable asking a committer to read 0002.

precedents_retrieved.title: Better tracking of free space during SP-GiST index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that SP-GiST index build track several recently used pages per page category instead of only the last one, so that free space is reused better. A fixed table gives more cache slots to leaf pages than to other categories.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the patch, and Tomas Vondra called it a solid improvement. After review, Tom Lane planned to make page selection by free space more efficient. He did not have time for that before the commitfest ended, so he asked for the entry to be marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I doubt I will get to it this week, so let's mark it RWF for this fest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Sort leaf pages by ctid for gist indexes built using sorting method
precedents_retrieved.summary: For GiST indexes built with the sorted (sortsupport) build method, the patch sorts index tuples on leaf pages by heap TID, so that leaf order follows heap order as it does for indexes built by repeated inserts. The goal was to avoid reading the same heap page more than once and to improve prefetching during scans.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only reply, from Andrey Borodin, supported the idea, measured roughly a 5% slowdown in CREATE INDEX, and asked for benchmarks showing the scan benefit. The entry was withdrawn the next day with no further message shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: amcheck verification for GiST
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GiST verification function to contrib/amcheck that checks parent/child key consistency and that all leaf pages are at the same depth. Later versions hold buffer locks on parent and child pages together and take only an AccessShareLock on the relation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan questioned whether the checks are safe under an AccessShareLock, since Heikki's v6 had used a ShareLock. He doubted that the parent re-find logic copied from gistfinishsplit() applies here and asked how concurrent page deletion could affect it. Andrey Borodin did not answer these questions for about two months, so Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: My main concern now is the heavyweight lock strength needed by the new function.

precedents_retrieved.title: GIN fillfactor
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fillfactor storage parameter to GIN indexes so that index build leaves free space on pages, and apply it to the page split ratio in dataPlaceToPageLeaf. The default was debated between 100, which matches the packed 9.4 indexes, and 90.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No benchmark showed that the option improves performance. Heikki Linnakangas tested random updates and found that GIN indexes do not bloat after build, because posting tree pages already keep some free space, so he concluded the option is not useful in practice. Alexander Korotkov showed one case with bloat but agreed it was probably not worth it without real use cases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on this, I think we should just drop this patch. It's not useful in
practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: [doc] vacuum full, fillfactor, and "extra space"
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the VACUUM FULL text in the VACUUM reference page so that it no longer says the table is rewritten "with no extra space". It moves VACUUM FULL to its own paragraph and says the new file keeps free space as set by fillfactor.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut found the new text no clearer: it made VACUUM FULL sound as if its main purpose were to leave fillfactor room, and he preferred keeping "no extra space" with fillfactor in a parenthetical note. The author did not reply to his review or to later reminders, so the entry stayed Waiting on Author and was closed as Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The fillfactor stuff
is valid to be mentioned, but the way it's being proposed makes it sound
like the main purpose of VACUUM FULL is to bloat the table to make
fillfactor room.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fillfactor for GIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add fillfactor as a storage parameter for GIN indexes, controlling how full pages are packed at index build time and, in later versions, the split ratio of posting-tree pages. Revised versions applied fillfactor only to posting trees and debated whether the default should be 100 (matching 9.4 index sizes) or 90 (matching btree).
precedents_retrieved.objection: No test results or benchmarks were provided showing that a fillfactor parameter improves GIN index performance, although an earlier reviewer had asked for them and got no reply. Robert Haas objected on that basis. The author agreed that no such benchmark existed and that he had no time to work on it soon, and asked for the patch to be rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There's only value in adding a fillfactor parameter to GIN indexes if
it improves performance.  There are no benchmarks showing it does.

precedents_retrieved.title: Pageinspect - add functions on GIN and GiST indexes from gevel
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Tomas Vondra, Ashutosh Sharma, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves the gevel module's functions for GiST, SP-GiST and GIN indexes into pageinspect, with tests and docs. The functions show whole-index statistics, print the tree and its stored objects, and estimate GIN value counts and query matches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers said the functions read the whole index, while pageinspect inspects single pages, so the code belongs in a new extension or should be rewritten as page-level functions. Peter Eisentraut also found that the patch no longer compiled and that the stats functions returned one formatted text value where they should return a row with columns. The author planned a new contrib module but posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback after three weeks of waiting on the author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The proposed patch uses a very different approach, reading the whole index,
not individual pages. Why should it be part of pageinspect?

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes honoring fillfactor in sorted GiST builds. The GIN fillfactor rejections apply only in part, because the option already exists for GiST.
Two objections, both about how existing settings behave after the change. The basic goal, making the reloption behave as documented, fits existing practice for other index types.

The proposal changes only how a sorted GiST build fills pages, and the page layout stays the same, so existing indexes stay valid and pg_upgrade copies them unchanged. Standbys replay the built pages as before, and the visible material shows no catalog, WAL record, protocol or ABI change. The default fillfactor of 90 may grow sorted-built indexes and their build WAL after reindex; that is a size and performance question for another angle.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Only the index owner can set fillfactor with alter index or create index, and the larger index at low fillfactor is the same kind of growth that buffering GiST builds and btree fillfactor already allow, so no new privilege, information leak or denial-of-service path appears.

The idea is small and makes an existing reloption work as documented, so no fatal objection from this angle. The objections above ask for measurements and do not dispute the goal. The GIN fillfactor precedents [P6] and [P8] are not cited: they added a new option, while this patch makes an existing one work.
One objection from this angle. No known extension provides this, and the existing workaround is slower, so the gap is convenience and build speed, not capability.
Two demand objections stand. Fixing the documentation gap, for example by stating that sorted builds ignore fillfactor, remains a cheap alternative until demand is shown.
